instruction: Design a small AUTOSAR cybersecurity utility in MISRA-C style that safely adds two uint8 values without wrapping.
input: The function shall saturate at UINT8_MAX, have no dynamic memory allocation, and return a deterministic result for every input.

instruction: Generate an AUTOSAR software component specification for a vehicle speed monitor that raises OverspeedWarning above 100 km/h.
input: Use one periodic runnable named VehicleSpeedMonitor_Run with a 10 ms period. The input is VehicleSpeed in km/h and the output is a boolean OverspeedWarning.
output:
SWC: VehicleSpeedMonitor

Ports:
  RequiredData:
    - VehicleSpeed: uint16, km/h
  ProvidedData:
    - OverspeedWarning: boolean

Runnable:
  Name: VehicleSpeedMonitor_Run
  Trigger: TimingEvent
  Period: 10 ms

Behavior:
  if VehicleSpeed > 100
      OverspeedWarning = TRUE
  else
      OverspeedWarning = FALSE

Requirements:
  - The runnable shall update OverspeedWarning on every activation.
  - A speed of exactly 100 km/h shall not trigger the warning.

instruction: Create an AUTOSAR SWC specification for a brake pedal status component.
input: Read BrakePedalPosition as a percentage from 0 to 100. Set BrakeApplied to TRUE at or above 5 percent. Reject values above 100 percent by reporting an invalid input status.
output:
SWC: BrakePedalMonitor

Ports:
  RequiredData:
    - BrakePedalPosition: uint8, percent
  ProvidedData:
    - BrakeApplied: boolean
    - BrakePedalInputValid: boolean

Runnable:
  Name: BrakePedalMonitor_Run
  Trigger: TimingEvent
  Period: 10 ms

Behavior:
  if BrakePedalPosition > 100
      BrakePedalInputValid = FALSE
      BrakeApplied = FALSE
  else
      BrakePedalInputValid = TRUE
      BrakeApplied = (BrakePedalPosition >= 5)

instruction: Generate AUTOSAR diagnostic behavior for a coolant over-temperature monitor.
input: CoolantTemperature is an int16 value in degrees Celsius. Set DTC_CoolantOverTemperature when the temperature is above 120 degrees for three consecutive 100 ms samples. Clear the pending counter when the temperature returns to 120 or below.
output:
SWC: CoolantTemperatureMonitor

Input:
  CoolantTemperature: int16, degrees Celsius

DiagnosticEvent:
  Name: DTC_CoolantOverTemperature
  Debounce: 3 consecutive failed samples
  SamplePeriod: 100 ms

Runnable:
  CoolantTemperatureMonitor_Run

Logic:
  if CoolantTemperature > 120
      OverTemperatureCounter = OverTemperatureCounter + 1
  else
      OverTemperatureCounter = 0

  if OverTemperatureCounter >= 3
      ReportDiagnosticEvent(DTC_CoolantOverTemperature, FAILED)
  else
      ReportDiagnosticEvent(DTC_CoolantOverTemperature, PASSED)

instruction: Define an AUTOSAR CAN signal handling specification for a vehicle speed signal.
input: The signal VehicleSpeedRaw is uint16, has a factor of 0.01 km/h per bit, and is received in CAN message VehicleStatus every 20 ms. A timeout after 100 ms shall mark the signal invalid and use a safe value of zero.
output:
Signal: VehicleSpeed

Network:
  Message: VehicleStatus
  CycleTime: 20 ms
  Timeout: 100 ms

Conversion:
  RawType: uint16
  PhysicalType: float32
  Factor: 0.01 km/h per bit
  Offset: 0.0 km/h

Runnable:
  VehicleSpeed_Update

Behavior:
  on VehicleStatus received
      VehicleSpeed = VehicleSpeedRaw * 0.01
      VehicleSpeedValid = TRUE
      ResetTimeoutTimer()

  on timeout
      VehicleSpeed = 0.0
      VehicleSpeedValid = FALSE

instruction: Create an AUTOSAR watchdog supervision specification for a periodic application runnable.
input: The runnable PowertrainControl_Run is expected every 10 ms. It must complete within 5 ms. Report a supervision failure after two consecutive missed or late executions.
output:
SWC: PowertrainControl

Runnable:
  Name: PowertrainControl_Run
  ExpectedPeriod: 10 ms
  MaximumExecutionTime: 5 ms

WatchdogSupervision:
  Type: Alive and deadline supervision
  AllowedMissedExecutions: 1
  FailureThreshold: 2 consecutive violations

Behavior:
  - Start execution monitoring when PowertrainControl_Run begins.
  - Stop execution monitoring when PowertrainControl_Run completes.
  - Report WdgM_LocalStatus as OK for valid executions.
  - Report WdgM_LocalStatus as FAILED after two consecutive period or deadline violations.

instruction: Create a small AUTOSAR MCAL DIO wrapper in MISRA-C style.
input: Read one configured Dio channel and return the channel level through an output pointer. Reject a null output pointer. Do not allocate memory or use global state.

instruction: Specify an AUTOSAR DCM DID configuration for reading a vehicle identification number.
input: Configure DID 0xF190 to return exactly 17 ASCII bytes from a VIN provider. Permit reads in the default and extended diagnostic sessions. Reject unsupported sessions and never return a partial VIN.
output:
DCM DID: 0xF190
Service: UDS ReadDataByIdentifier (0x22)
Data length: 17 bytes
Data type: ASCII
Provider: VIN data provider runnable
Allowed sessions: DefaultSession, ExtendedDiagnosticSession
Behavior:
- Return all 17 bytes only when the provider reports valid data.
- Reject requests from unsupported sessions with the configured NRC.
- Do not expose partially initialized or stale VIN data.
- Map the DID and session references to project-defined DCM configuration definitions.

instruction: Define DEM event debouncing for a coolant over-temperature diagnostic event.
input: Sample coolant temperature every 100 ms. A temperature above 120 degrees Celsius is a failed sample. Confirm the event after three consecutive failed samples; reset the failure counter after any passing sample.
output:
Diagnostic event: CoolantOverTemperature
Event ID: project-assigned symbolic ID
Failure condition: CoolantTemperature > 120 degrees Celsius
Debounce: counter-based, increment on failed sample and reset on passed sample
Confirmation threshold: 3 consecutive failed samples
Runnable period: 100 ms
Behavior:
- Report DEM_EVENT_STATUS_FAILED when the threshold is reached.
- Report DEM_EVENT_STATUS_PASSED for a passing sample.
- Saturate the counter at the confirmation threshold to prevent overflow.
- Bind the event to the project DTC and configured operation cycle.

instruction: Create an NvM block configuration specification for a persistent ECU setting.
input: Store a 16-byte calibration setting in a nonvolatile block. Restore its configured default at startup if the stored block is invalid. Trigger writes only after an explicit application update request.
output:
NvM block: CalibrationSettingBlock
Payload size: 16 bytes
RAM mirror: CalibrationSettingRam
Startup behavior:
- Request block restoration during initialization.
- If the stored block is invalid, load the configured default and report the invalid-block status.
Write behavior:
- Do not write periodically.
- Issue an NvM write request only after the application update request.
- Check the asynchronous request result before reporting persistence success.
- Use project-assigned block identifiers and generated NvM configuration references.

instruction: Specify SecOC protection for a periodic CAN status message.
input: Authenticate the complete configured CAN payload and freshness value. Reject messages with an invalid authenticator or stale freshness value. Use the project security profile and keys; do not define or embed key material.
output:
SecOC protected PDU: VehicleStatus
Protection: authenticate configured payload and freshness value
Authenticator: use the algorithm, truncation, and key references from the approved project security profile
Freshness: use the configured freshness value manager and acceptance window
Receiver behavior:
- Verify the authenticator before delivering the PDU to the application.
- Reject invalid authenticators and stale or repeated freshness values.
- Report verification failures through the configured diagnostic path.
- Never store key material in generated source code or ARXML literals.

instruction: Define CAN Network Management behavior for a control unit that should sleep when the network is idle.
input: On a network request, enter the network-requested state and keep communication active. After the last request is released, follow the configured Nm timeout and enter ready-sleep, then bus-sleep when permitted. A received network request cancels pending sleep.
output:
Module: CanNm
Network request:
- Enter the network-requested state.
- Keep the configured communication channels active.
Last request released:
- Start the configured Nm timeout.
- Enter ready-sleep after the timeout expires.
- Enter bus-sleep only when the configured shutdown conditions are met.
Wake-up:
- A valid received network request cancels pending sleep and resumes network operation.
Configuration note: use generated channel, timing, and PDU references; do not hard-code project-specific identifiers.

instruction: Generate three separate artifacts for a simple AUTOSAR brake-pedal monitor: a C header, C source, and a well-formed AUTOSAR 4.x ARXML package skeleton.
input: Input is an unsigned 8-bit pedal percentage. Values above 100 are invalid; BrakeApplied is true at 5 percent or higher. The C API shall reject null output pointers and use no dynamic allocation. Keep the ARXML as a minimal package skeleton without invented implementation references.
